C1.worst_defect: The home page says clearly what this is ("Point of sale for Vendure", "Pre-release · plugin 0.3.0"), but it never says who should not use it or how it compares with a hosted till (Shopify POS, Square, Lightspeed). It also names no maintainer or company: the footer only says "MIT licensed. Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS." The ten identical "What it does today" cards give no sense of which features matter most.
C1.where: home.desktop.01-02 (hero, 'What it does today'), home footer

C2.worst_defect: The footer says "MIT licensed", and the site presents the till as something you can build and host yourself, yet 'Before you start' says "To build and host it yourself ... you need your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)". No page says this is a paid, proprietary licence or what it costs. Other doubts: three releases in five days (0.1.0 on 2026-10-01; 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 both on 2026-10-06), then nothing for six weeks. The known "no ReadOrder" role bug is documented in four places instead of being fixed in a 0.3.1. The demo has refund at the till, which the table marks "No, not on plugin 0.3.0", with no note on when or whether it will be released.
C2.where: home.desktop.02 'Before you start'; limitations; changelog; home 'Live demo or your own store' table

C3.worst_defect: The guide is complete and in the right order, but the plugin's auto-created role misses a permission, so the reader must patch it by hand ("Also add ReadOrder"). A leftover collapsible, "If your store already allows vendurepos.vercel.app", names an old origin that a new user will never have.

C4.worst_defect: The changelog is written for the authors, not for store owners ("order.create v5 ... (ADR 0005)"). The troubleshooting caveat that refused register closures and cash records "do not reach your Vendure store from this till" is buried in a dense paragraph, though it is the most important thing a store owner needs to know about losing data.

C5.worst_defect: The hero till screenshot is cropped through the middle of a product row. The 'What it does today' grid is ten identical cards with no visual hierarchy. Apart from at-the-till, every docs page is text only. Dark mode holds up.

C6.worst_defect: On the phone, the hero app screenshot shrinks until a column header is cut to "Q..." and the "Add charge" button is clipped, so the one picture of the product looks broken. The docs pages reflow well (the tax table becomes stacked cards and the code wraps).

C7.worst_defect: The technical surface is strong: every page returns 200, the 404 is a real 404, the JSON-LD and llms.txt are present, and Lighthouse scores 97-98 for performance and 100 elsewhere. Minor faults: 52 KiB of unused JS and a 120 ms render-blocking resource, LCP of 2.6 s on quick-start, and every sitemap lastmod set to the capture date, which makes the dates meaningless.

overall_worst.defect: "MIT licensed" is the headline licence claim, but building and hosting the till yourself needs "your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)", and no page says that licence is paid and proprietary or what it costs. A sceptic who finds this after reading the footer will distrust the rest of the open-source framing.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 'Before you start' and home footer; limitations
overall_worst.fix: Next to "MIT licensed" and in 'Before you start', say plainly that self-building needs a commercial RxDB Premium licence, link to its pricing, and say that the hosted till at app.vendurepos.com needs no licence of your own.
